answer: Persistent channel fingerprinting binds each identity to a unique radio or timing signature observed continuously, so a bot farm cannot present one identity at a tide of concurrent connections without collisions. The rule enforces one live session per fingerprint and flags duplicates before they transact. An attacker must acquire physically distinct hardware per identity, and rotating fingerprints costs a fresh device plus calibration time that compounds each dawn. Cloning a single operator's fingerprint fails at the first comet of synchronized activity.
